changes.text: 1916年七月底八月初，在美国留学的胡适给自己定了一条规矩：不再写旧诗词，只用白话作诗；诗集名字他都想好了，叫《尝试集》。可他一向说自己是保守的人，认为语言文字是世界上最保守的东西，比宗教还保守，还说这一路是被「逼上梁山」的——这句成语说的是一个人为环境所迫，不得已而做出违反他本意的非常行为。

In late July and early August of 1916, Hu Shi, a Chinese student in America, gave himself a rule: no more old-style verse. He would write poetry only in baihua, the everyday spoken language, and he had already named the book to come — Changshi ji, or Experiments. Yet he called himself a conservative: language and writing, he liked to say, are the most conservative things in the world, more conservative than religion. And he said he had been pushed here — bi shang Liangshan, driven to Liangshan, an idiom for someone forced by circumstances into extraordinary acts against his own intentions.
按他自己的说法，把他推到这一步的，不是什么大事件，而是一首送别诗引起的小小偶然事件，和朋友之间持续一年多的争吵。争的是白话能不能用来写文学：到1916年夏天，朋友们已承认白话可以写小说、演说，唯独不肯承认它能作诗——反对者已经退到只剩一处：诗。

In his own telling, what pushed him was no great event, but a small accident set off by a farewell poem, and a quarrel among friends that ran on for over a year. The quarrel was over whether the vernacular could serve literature. By the summer of 1916 his friends granted it would do for fiction and speeches, but not for poetry. Poetry was the last fortress.

更早的引子，藏在每月的支票信封里。庚款留学生每月从华盛顿的清华学生监督处收到一张支票，主办的书记钟文鳌——一位教会学校出身、热心改革社会风俗的好好先生——总在信封里夹一张小传单，上面写着「不满二十五岁不娶妻。」「废除汉字，改用字母！」「多种树，种树有益。」之类的话。平时大家随手把它丢进纸篓。约在1915年，胡适却坐下来回了一张很不客气的字条，大意是：像你这样既不懂汉字、又不能写汉文的人，「你最好闭起鸟嘴！」

The first trigger hid in a monthly check. Chinese students on the Boxer Indemnity scholarship drew their stipend from the Tsinghua student-supervision office in Washington, and inside every envelope was a leaflet slipped in by the clerk who mailed it: Zhong Wen'ao, a kindly man from the missionary school St. John's in Shanghai, who was keen to reform Chinese society. Its slogans ran, in translation: marry no one under twenty-five; abolish the Chinese characters and switch to an alphabet; plant more trees, for trees do good. Usually it went straight into the wastebasket. Around 1915 Hu sat down and wrote back a rude little note, which ran roughly, in translation: a man like you, who neither understands the characters nor can write the language, had better shut his beak.

字条寄出后他心中懊悔，觉得不该对一位和善又有心改革语言文字的人如此不礼貌，于是在朋友面前自我谴责，并想到一层：假如钟君这样的人不够资格谈这个问题，那么够资格的人实在更该认真研究，把可行与不可行的问题都摆出来检讨。他找上1910年同进康乃尔的赵元任，两人商定把“中国文字的问题”作为美东中国学生会文学股年会的论题，各写一篇：赵元任论吾国文字能否采用字母制及其进行方法，他论“如何可使吾国文言易于教授”。

After the note was sent, he regretted it. Zhong was a kind man with a sincere wish to reform Chinese customs and writing; the rudeness was uncalled for, and Hu reproached himself before his friends. Then a further thought: if men like Zhong are not qualified to discuss such questions, then the qualified should do the work — set out what is feasible and what is not, and examine both. He took it up with Zhao Yuanren, who had entered Cornell with him in 1910. They agreed to make "the question of China's writing" the literature section's topic for the annual meeting of the Chinese Students' Association in the East, and split it: Zhao on whether the Chinese script could adopt an alphabetic system and how to proceed; Hu on "how to make our classical written language easier to teach."
这句“作诗如作文”引来一场是非。梅、任都参战，梅光迪认为诗之文字与文之文字自诗文以来（不论中西）早已分道而驰，根本不能混为一谈。辩论不休，牵涉愈多，内容愈复杂：用胡适自己的话说，朋友们愈辩愈保守，他也愈辩愈激进。

Thus the slogan — write poetry like prose — started a fight. Mei and Ren both weighed in. Poetry and prose, Mei held, could never be mixed: poetic diction and prose diction had parted ways since each began, in China and the West alike. The debate never stopped, and the further it ran the more it dragged in. As Hu put it, the more his friends argued the more conservative they grew; the more he argued, the more radical.

转机出现在1916年二三月。他形成一个概括观念：整部中国文学史就是一部文学工具变迁史，一个工具替代另一个工具；同时也是一部活文学逐渐代替死文学的历史。工具一旦活力消失、逐渐僵化，就要换一个，在这种嬗递中接受一个活的工具，他称之为“文学革命”。三月，他写长信给在麻州剑桥、正在哈佛的梅光迪，说中古以后老的语言工具已不够用，变迁在唐代便已发生：散文体裁发生革命，逐渐发展出以白话表达的语录体，先为和尚们采用，后来宋代哲学家用它记录哲学讨论，老百姓又用它作歌曲、编戏剧、写短篇和长篇小说。他说用白话写的活文学——最明显的如元曲——是民众不知不觉中完成的文学革命的最高潮，中国文学之复苏实得力于白话戏曲和白话小说之兴起。出乎他意料，这套由历史分析得出的结论，竟被这位保守朋友欣然接受。需要补一句：他们当时以为传统长篇小说都是元代作品，胡适本人晚年更正说，《水浒》一流的故事流传几百年，到明代才写成定稿。

The turn came in February and March of 1916. Hu reached a general idea: the history of Chinese literature is a history of changing literary tools, one replacing another, and at the same time a history of living literature gradually displacing dead literature. When a tool loses its vitality and hardens it must be changed, and taking up a living tool in that succession is what he called literary revolution. In March he wrote a long letter to Mei, then at Harvard in Cambridge, Massachusetts: after the medieval period the old language tool could no longer carry people's thoughts, and the change had begun in the Tang, when prose style was revolutionized and a vernacular recorded-sayings style grew up — taken up first by monks, later by Song philosophers for their discussions, and then by ordinary people for songs, plays, stories and novels. Vernacular literature of that kind, Yuan drama most obviously, was, he said, the climax of a literary revolution the masses completed without knowing it; the revival of Chinese literature owed much to the rise of vernacular drama and fiction. To Hu's surprise, this conclusion drawn from historical analysis was gladly accepted by his conservative friend. One note: they then took the great traditional novels for Yuan works; Hu corrected himself in later years, saying that stories like Water Margin circulated for centuries before being written down in final form under the Ming.
1916年7月6日，他在日记里写下九条主张，头两条是「今日之文言乃是一种半死的文字。」和「今日之白话是一种活的语言。」他说这九条很确切地表达了他策动中国文学革命的中心思想；又说这许多严肃的讨论和历史性的研析，其实都只源于一首送别诗引起的小小偶然事件。

Then the diary. On July 6, 1916, he set down nine propositions; the first two, in translation: the classical written language of today is a half-dead form of writing; the vernacular of today is a living language. These nine, he said, expressed precisely the central ideas behind his launching of China's literary revolution — and all these serious discussions and historical analyses came out of one small accident, a farewell poem to a friend going to Harvard.

两天之后，凯约嘉湖上出了桩险事。7月8日，任鸿隽、沃莎女子学院的学生陈衡哲、梅光迪、杨铨、唐钺等人在湖上划船，片云头上黑，忽然刮起风暴，雨落下来，他们急忙往岸边划，几乎把船弄翻，个个淋得狼狈不堪。对这批中国留学生来说，这也算件险事。任鸿隽随后写了一首四言古诗《泛湖即事》附在信里，请胡适批评。诗中用了《诗经》里“言”字一类的老字，而胡适此前恰好写过一篇《言字解》。他不喜欢这种陈腐文字与现代语言夹杂，回信说此诗不好，因为「文字殊不调和」，又有「三千年前之死语」之说。任鸿隽不服，愤愤不平；更有意思的是另一位哈佛朋友梅光迪路见不平，写来一封十分激动的信反击。梅当时正受保守派批评家白璧德的影响，对胡适的一切激进主张都反对到底：他认为语言必须经过第一流的诗人加以锻炼，才能成为诗的语言；文学的文字、尤其是诗的文字，一定要由第一流的诗人和美术家加以美化，才能成为诗之文字。他据此对胡适的观念大加挞伐。

Two days later, another accident. On July 8 Ren Hongjun, Chen Hengzhe of Vassar, Mei Guangdi, Yang Quan, Tang Yue and others were rowing on Cayuga Lake when a black cloud gathered overhead, a storm broke and the rain fell; pulling for shore in a hurry they nearly capsized, and all came away soaked and dishevelled. For that band of Chinese students it was a real adventure, and Ren wrote it up in Fanhu jishi (Boating on the Lake), an old four-character-style poem he mailed to Hu for criticism. It used archaic words such as the particle yan, of the kind found in the Book of Songs — Hu had earlier written an essay on that very word — and he disliked dead diction mixed with modern language. He wrote back that the poem was bad because its wording was thoroughly incongruous, and he spoke of dead language of three thousand years ago (both paraphrased from the Chinese). Ren was indignant. More interesting was the letter that followed: Mei, his other friend at Harvard, riding to the rescue in high dudgeon. Under the influence of his conservative teacher Babbitt, Mei opposed all of Hu's radicalism to the end — language becomes poetic only after first-rate poets refine it, and the language of literature, poetry above all, must be beautified by first-rate poets and artists before it counts as poetic diction. On that ground he lashed Hu's ideas.

胡适的回应是一首约一百句的滑稽打油诗，他生平写的最长的一首：开头描写老梅大发脾气，再举许多例子开玩笑地驳“文字哪有死活”，并顺着对方的论点反将一军——文字须经诗人长期锻炼，这正是他想做的事，当代的诗人作家正该把这些俗语俗字锻炼起来，提高它们的地位，把它们提到诗歌文学里来。两位朋友读了大发雷霆，复信取笑他企图作白话诗，但胡适在信里发现两人有个共同的论调：白话的生动可以用在评话、故事、长篇小说等写作上，就是不能用在诗里。梅光迪说的范围更宽：在小说和民歌里白话可以用，但在高级散文里——肯定的是在诗里面——白话千万用不得；任鸿隽说得最干脆：「白话自有白话用处（如作小说、演说等），然不能用之于诗！」按胡适的归纳，朋友们在其他方面都已让步，只剩诗这一处还在争。

Hu answered with a comic doggerel poem of about a hundred lines, the longest he ever wrote: Old Mei in a towering rage, examples piled up to mock the theory that words have no life or death, and Mei's own argument turned against him — if words must be forged by poets over long practice, that is exactly what he wanted. Contemporary poets and writers should take these vulgar, colloquial words, temper them, raise their standing and bring them into poetry. The burlesque threw both friends into a fury; both wrote back to mock his attempt at vernacular verse, yet Hu found a common line in their letters: the liveliness of the vernacular could serve storytelling, tales and novels, but not poetry. Mei drew the line more widely: the vernacular was usable in fiction and folk songs, but in high prose — and certainly in poetry — it must never be used. Ren was bluntest; his letter said, in translation, that the vernacular has its own uses, such as novels and speeches, but cannot be used for poetry. As Hu summed it up, his friends had given way everywhere else; only poetry was still in dispute.
于是问题收缩成一个点。胡适把反对理由排了队：第一，从来没有诗人用俗语俗字作过诗，他在中国诗词中只找到一首、甚至一首中的几句是白话，白话诗数量太少，这使朋友们振振有词；第二，也是朋友们更能言之成理的一条，从来没有中国作家认真着实用白话作诗，多半是兴之所至偶写几行，骨子里对白话有下意识的鄙弃。他的结论是：要说服朋友相信白话可以作诗，只有以身作则，认真尝试用白话作诗，除此之外没有别的办法。

And so the dispute narrowed to a point: the vernacular for every department of literature except poetry. Hu ranked the objections. First, no poet had written in vulgar words and everyday speech — in Chinese poetry he could find one poem, perhaps a few lines of one; the scarcity of vernacular poems gave his friends their confident case. Second, and the more persuasive for his friends, no Chinese writer had seriously tried: a few vernacular lines in a fit of high spirits, no more, and beneath that a half-conscious contempt. To convince them there was one course only — set an example, seriously try to write vernacular poetry. Nothing else would do.

1916年十一月，他把一年多讨论的结果写成文章，提出八条很温和的建议，题目用的是“改良”和“刍议”。据他事后解释，“文学革命”一词在他自己的诗和信里、朋友给他的来信里早已常见，有时是开玩笑，有时也很严肃；但第一次把结论送到国内发表时，他考虑到老一辈保守分子无可怀疑的反对，刻意把文题写得温和而谦虚。文章誊了三份：一份交给他自己主编、当时由商务印书馆承印的《中国留美学生季报》，一份寄给陈独秀主编、已出版数年的《新青年》；陈独秀于1916年受聘为国立北京大学文科学长。

In November 1916 he shaped more than a year of argument into an article with eight very moderate suggestions. Even the title was modest: he dropped "literary revolution," a phrase that had come up often in his own poems and letters and in his friends' letters to him, sometimes in jest and sometimes in earnest. This was the first time the conclusions would be sent home to China for publication, and, in view of the undoubted resistance of the older conservatives, he kept the wording gentle — reform, not revolution; a humble opinion, not dogma. Three copies: one to the Chinese Students' Quarterly he edited in America, then printed by the Commercial Press; one to New Youth, which Chen Duxiu — from 1916 dean of arts at National Peking University — had been editing for several years.

1917年一月，文章在《新青年》刊出，文化界反应很大。北大有两位教授重视它：一位是陈独秀本人，本是死硬派的革命人物，随后写《文学革命论》响应，公开支持文学革命，并说首举义旗的是朋友胡适，自己高张大旗作声援；另一位是古典音韵学教授、章太炎门人钱玄同，这位古文大家没有写文章，却写去小批评大捧场的长信，也在《新青年》发表，声势为之一振。赵元任则常说胡适的白话诗文“不够白”，不是一般人常用的真正语体；胡适承认了，打了个比方：像裹了四十年或者二十年小脚的女人，纵使把小脚放大，终究恢复不了天足。

It appeared in New Youth in January 1917 and stirred a great response. Two Peking University professors took it seriously. Chen Duxiu, an unbending revolutionary, answered with "On Literary Revolution," publicly backing a literary revolution and saying frankly that the banner had been raised by his friend Hu Shi; he was only hoisting a flag in support. Qian Xuantong, professor of classical phonology, a master of ancient prose and a disciple of the great scholar Zhang Taiyan, wrote no article but sent Chen and Hu long letters — small criticisms, great praise — also printed in New Youth; that so eminent a classicist should sympathize buoyed their cause. Zhao Yuanren often said that Hu's vernacular poems and essays were "not vernacular enough," not the genuine spoken style ordinary people used. Hu admitted it: like a woman who had bound her feet for forty, or even twenty, years, however much she loosened the bindings she would never recover natural feet.

作者推断：他选择以身作则，并不只是姿态，而是把分歧改造成可检验的问题。“白话不能用之于诗”是个全称判断，理论上一首像样的白话诗就能动摇它；反之，没有诗，再多书信也只是意见相持。他把新诗集提前定名《尝试集》，等于当众揽下举证责任，把胜负交给一场公开、长期、别人看得见的试验。一种解释是，这也呼应了译注者唐德刚对他的定位——夹在必然与偶然之间的“实验主义者”，不肯听任事情自然演变，而要在试验中寻找方向。不过「没有“胡适”，恐怕也就没有“白话文运动”——至少运动也不会在那时就发生了」是唐德刚的评论，不是可核实的史实。

The author's inference: his decision to lead by example was not merely a pose; it converted a disagreement into a testable question. The claim that the vernacular cannot be used for poetry is a universal one, and one decent vernacular poem is enough in principle to shake it; without a poem, letters could go on forever as a standoff of opinions. By naming the collection Experiments in advance, he publicly took on the burden of proof and left the outcome to a long, open trial that others could watch. One reading is that this matches the translator-editor Tang Degang's portrait of him as a pragmatist standing between necessity and chance, unwilling to let events drift and determined to search out the right direction through experiment. Still, Tang's remark — in paraphrase, that without Hu Shi there would probably have been no Vernacular Movement, or at least it would not have happened then — is commentary, not verifiable history.
结局也可以交代一笔。胡适自述，运动约四年就在学校教育上基本成功：1920年北京政府教育部通令，国民小学一、二年级教材一律改用白话，旧教材分期废除。但他称之为“部分的胜利”，重要的部分是以白话为教育工具；他同时说，1919年的学生运动把文化运动变成了政治运动，对文艺复兴运动是一种“干扰”，虽则对传播白话文功不可没。

The outcome can be set down too. By Hu's account, in only about four years the effort to replace the classical language with the vernacular in the schools had all but succeeded: in 1920 the Ministry of Education of the Beijing government ordered that all first- and second-year textbooks in the national primary schools be written entirely in the vernacular, with the old textbooks abolished in stages. Yet he called it only a partial victory; the important part was making the vernacular the instrument of education. He also said the student movement of 1919 had been an interruption to the Renaissance movement, turning a cultural movement into a political one, though it did much to spread the vernacular.
本文材料只来自一本书：胡适口述、唐德刚译注《胡适口述自传》（中国文史出版社2020年）。按唐德刚说明，这一章英文稿是从《四十自述》中《逼上梁山》一节节译、经胡适手订后又回译成中文的，与原文多少有点出入。因此这是当事人多年后的自述，不是当时的独立记录；梅光迪、任鸿隽的反应和话语，都经胡适转述，本文不推测他们的内心。

The material here comes from one book only: Hu Shi's oral memoir, translated and annotated by Tang Degang, The Oral Memoir of Hu Shi (Chinese Literature and History Press, 2020). As Tang explains, the English draft of this chapter was abridged from the Bi shang Liangshan (Driven to Liangshan) section of Hu's Forty Self-Narratives, revised in Hu's own hand, then translated back into Chinese — and it differs from the original in some degree. This is therefore a participant's account given many years later, not an independent record from the time. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's reactions and their words all reach us through Hu's retelling, and this piece does not speculate about their inner thoughts.

几处需要降级看待：他为何用“改良”不用“革命”，是本人事后的解释；唐德刚关于“实验主义者”“鸡蛋与鸡，必然和偶然是说不清的”等说法，都是译注者的评论；对“文言是半死的文字”这句口号，唐德刚认为它当年有摧枯拉朽的功能，但真实性值得重新商榷。白话文与白话诗的结局也不同：按唐德刚的说法，白话文是百分之百成功，白话诗则未必——至少还未脱离“尝试”阶段。文中主要日期依据本书：约1915年（胡适说“我想是”）、1916年二三月、1916年三月、7月6日、7月8日、7月26日、7月底8月初、1916年十一月、1917年一月。

A few things should be read with lowered confidence. Why he used reform rather than revolution is his own retrospective explanation. Tang Degang's remarks about the pragmatist and about the chicken and the egg — necessity and chance are impossible to disentangle — are the annotator's commentary, not fact. On the slogan that the classical language is a half-dead form of writing, Tang thought it had a devastating force in its day but that its truth is worth debating again. The two outcomes also differ: in Tang's judgment vernacular prose was a hundred per cent successful, while vernacular poetry was not necessarily so — at least it has not yet left the experimental stage. The main dates used here follow the book: around 1915 (Hu's own hedge: I think it was); February and March 1916; March 1916; July 6; July 8; July 26; late July and early August; November 1916; January 1917.
还有几点作者的补白：文中说小说年代“元明之辨”的修正，来自胡适本人晚年的更正，本文只依据这一更正，未另行核验；至于“若无胡适则运动不会发生”这类反事实，只能当作唐德刚的看法，作者不作结论，也不替历史排演它没有走过的路。唐德刚也记下，反对胡适的人觉得他居功太多；1956年胡适在哈佛大学以这一论调讲演时，后来为他作传的格里德简直嗤之以鼻。

A few further notes from the author. The correction over the dating of the novels — Yuan versus Ming — comes from Hu's own later recantation; this piece relies on that correction alone and has not checked it further. Counterfactuals of the sort that without Hu Shi the movement would not have happened can only be treated as Tang Degang's opinion; the author draws no conclusion, and does not rehearse roads history did not take. Tang also records that Hu's opponents felt he claimed too much credit; when Hu gave this account in a 1956 lecture at Harvard, Jerome B. Grieder, later his biographer, simply scoffed at it.
本文只有胡适晚年口述一种来源，且经节译、手订与回译；梅光迪、任鸿隽的言行均为胡适转述，胡适对动机的说明是事后自述，唐德刚的注释属评论而非史实。凡标为 interpretation 的段落是作者推断，标为 modern 的段落是为今日读者虚构的场景，都不是本文所据材料的记述。

This piece rests on a single source: Hu Shi's oral memoir in later life, itself abridged, revised in his own hand and translated back. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's words and deeds reach us only through Hu's retelling; Hu's explanations of motive are retrospective; and Tang Degang's notes are commentary rather than fact. Paragraphs marked interpretation are the author's inferences, paragraphs marked modern are scenarios invented for readers today; neither is drawn from the material this piece relies on.
